AccessModifier.Definition: An access modifier controls the visibility of the code element it is applied to, determining which other code can reference it.

Accessor.Definition: An accessor defines how a property or indexer value is read or written.

ArgumentModifier.Definition: A keyword that modifies how the accompanying argument is passed at this call site, such as by reference or as an output value.

CompilationScope.Definition: A keyword that establishes the structural scope of the code that follows, such as declaring a namespace or setting a global context.

Constraint.Definition: A constraint keyword restricts which types are valid arguments for a generic type parameter.

DiscardPattern.Definition: The discard pattern {c:color-blue keyword bold}_{/c} matches any input value and is used as a {c:bold}catch-all{/c} option in pattern matching.

DiscardValue.Definition: The discard symbol {c:color-blue keyword bold}_{/c} indicates that a produced value is {c:bold}intentionally ignored{/c} in an assignment or {c:color-blue keyword}out{/c} argument.

Iterator.Definition: An iterator keyword is used to implement enumerator logic, producing sequence elements one at a time without building the entire collection up front.

MemberDeclarator.Definition: A member declarator keyword introduces a specific kind of member within a type, such as an event or an operator overload.

MemberModifier.Definition: A member modifier changes the behavior or constraints of the member it is applied to, such as making it {c:color-blue keyword}static{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}abstract{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}virtual{/c}, or {c:color-blue keyword}readonly{/c}.

ObjectConstruction.Definition: An object construction keyword creates a new instance of a type, allocating and initializing it in memory.

ParameterModifier.Definition: A keyword that changes how this parameter receives its value, such as requiring it to be passed by reference, as an output, or as a variable-length argument list.

QueryExpression.Definition: A query expression keyword is part of the LINQ query syntax and specifies an operation to perform on the data source, such as filtering, ordering, or grouping.

ResourceManagement.Definition: A keyword for controlling the lifetime of a resource, ensuring it is properly set up and cleaned up at the correct time.

SafetyContext.Definition: A safety context keyword changes how the compiler treats the associated block, either permitting or restricting low-level operations that could affect memory safety.

TypeDeclarator.Definition: A type declarator keyword introduces a type declaration and specifies what kind of type is being defined, such as a {c:color-blue keyword}class{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}struct{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}record{/c}, or {c:color-blue keyword}interface{/c}.

TypeModifier.Definition: A modifier that changes the capabilities, constraints, or usage rules of a type declaration, such as its inheritance behavior, storage characteristics, or visibility scope.

TypeSystem.Definition: A type system keyword specifies how a type or value is treated by the compiler, such as whether it is nullable, how it is stored, or how it relates to the type hierarchy.

UsingDirectiveModifier.Definition: A keyword that changes how a {c:color-blue keyword}using{/c} directive behaves, such as making it apply globally or importing the static members of a type.

ConditionalBranching.Definition: A conditional branching keyword evaluates a condition and directs execution down the appropriate code path based on the result.

ControlFlow.Definition: A control flow keyword alters the normal sequential execution of code, redirecting it based on conditions, exceptions, or the current program state.

ExceptionHandling.Definition: An exception handling keyword manages errors that occur at runtime, allowing them to be caught, handled, or propagated safely.

JumpStatement.Definition: A jump statement keyword immediately transfers execution to a different point in the program.

LoopStatement.Definition: A loop statement keyword marks the beginning of a construct that repeatedly executes based on a condition or over a sequence of values.

Concurrency.Definition: A concurrency keyword controls how code interacts with multiple threads or asynchronous tasks running at the same time.

PatternMatching.Definition: A pattern matching keyword is used to test whether a value satisfies a specific pattern, type, or condition.
